 Washington Spirit prepare for the NWSL semifinals as Audi Field hosts historic doubleheader
 By José Umaña 
 November 13, 2026 | 
 5:42 PM 
 | 
 Getty Images/Jamie Sabau 
 WASHINGTON, DC - NOVEMBER 08: Sandy MacIver #18 of Washington Spirit celebrates after winning the NWSL Quarterfinal match between Washington Spirit and Portland Thorns FC as part of the 2026 Playoffs at Audi Field on November 08, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Jamie Sabau/Getty Images) 
 The Washington Spirit will look to keep its championship hopes alive Saturday when the team faces the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals.
 The match was not going to take place at D.C.’s Audi Field, the Spirit’s home venue, because of a scheduling conflict with the Secretaries’ Cup college football game. Instead, team officials were prepared to have Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland, host the semifinal.
 Now, after days of negotiations and organizing, the playoff game will stay in D.C. as part of a historic doubleheader, marking the first same-day changeover of its kind for the 20,000-seat soccer stadium.
 ‘Find a way to do both’
 Major League Soccer team D.C. United, which owns Audi Field, agreed to host the Secretaries’ Cup in spring 2025, President of Business Operations Danita Johnson told WTOP. The Cup is a Division III college football game played between the United States Merchant Marine Academy and the United States Coast Guard Academy. It is considered the “small college version of the Army-Navy Game.”
 With the 2026 NWSL playoff schedule announced months later, ESPN reported that Spirit officials prepared contingency plans to head to Northwest Stadium if the team made the semifinal round. However, last-minute negotiations between the Spirit and D.C. United led to both sides reaching a deal to keep the Spirit in D.C.
 Johnson recalled speaking with United Chairman and CEO Jason Levien during the talks, and both agreed to keep both events at Audi Field.
 “He was like, ‘Find a way to do both,'” she said. “And the league and the Spirit and the academies were all flexible and great partners in working with us to make that happen.”
 The challenge was setting up the venue for both sports, but Johnson credits both sides being flexible with the layout and timing. The field will be lined up for both sports; to avoid confusion, the soccer lines will be yellow, and the football lines will be white. The bases for the field goal posts will be in place and padded during the soccer match.
 Johnson said United worked with the National Women’s Soccer League, which has similar procedures at other multisport venues, including Lumen Field in Seattle.
 The Spirit game will kick off at noon, and if the match ends in regulation, the stadium should clear out in about 30 minutes, which fits within the standard protocols at Audi Field, Johnson said. Gates are set to open for the Secretaries’ Cup at 3:30 p.m., a quick transition but enough time to put up signage around the stadium and assemble the goalposts, Johnson said.
 Should the soccer match go into extra time or a penalty shootout, kickoff — slated for 4:30 p.m. — will be delayed.
 “We’ll clear the building completely and then have the changeover where the Secretary’s Cup fans will have the opportunity to enter,” Johnson said. “We’re encouraging Spirit fans to stay for the cadets, and Secretaries’ Cup fans to come early and cheer on the Spirit.”
 Spirit officials tell WTOP they anticipate a sellout for its semifinal match, while a United spokesperson said about 7,000 tickets have been distributed for the college football game.
 Audi Field has two visiting locker rooms and one home team locker room, typically reserved for D.C. United. Johnson said the stadium has plans for the locker room situation to accommodate all four teams, and staffing numbers are set to handle Saturday’s doubleheader.
 “This shows the power of what can be accomplished when everyone works together and we look forward to a festive environment for both events,” Spirit CEO Kim Stone said in a statement.
 Third semifinal in a row
 On the field, the Washington Spirit is preparing for its third consecutive semifinal appearance following a dominant 4-1 win over the Portland Thorns. Trinity Rodman scored twice and added an assist as the Spirit offense muscled its way to score three times before halftime.
 “This is the type of team we want to be,” goalkeeper Sandy MacIver said on Sunday. “We want to be ruthless; we want to be dominant, and I think we showed that at both ends. When you have a game like this, you’ve got to be clinical in both boxes, and we did that today.”
 With D.C. hosting the NWSL Championship this year, Rodman conceded that players have thought about playing in a final at their home stadium. However, Rodman and head coach Adrián González agreed that the Spirit cannot overlook a Utah Royals side that upset No. 2-seeded San Diego and earned a 1-1 at Audi Field in March.
 “For us, the key this whole season has been to be present in what we are doing,” González said on Sunday. “Now we have time to rest, and tomorrow we are going to start thinking about the next one against Utah, and that is it. We will not be thinking about anything else.”
